name: watch-your-step
description: 🥾 Catches command traps BEFORE a tool call runs: a backtick or $40 inside double quotes, a mistyped home directory, a file truncated before it is read, zsh's '====' abort, a bare glob that matches nothing, bash-isms under zsh, a commit that would record conflict markers, a worktree removal that would destroy ignored files, a worktree created from a dirty checkout, ps/pgrep output that would print full process arguments, a stash that silently skips untracked files, an unquoted $var argument list that reads as an empty result, a branch deletion whose commits would vanish, and a git checkout/restore/reset --hard/clean -f that would discard uncommitted changes. Rules are data with tests; silent-corruption traps are blocked with the exact fix, the rest are warnings, and one visible '# wys:allow <rule>' overrides a single command.
